hints.text: Find the email values that occur more than once. Compare the exact stored text: case, leading or trailing spaces and inner spaces all make different values, and NULL is one group.
The survivor is the row with the lowest numeric id, not the earliest created_at and not the most recently created row.
Do not lowercase or trim the email. SQLite BINARY equality is the declared grouping, so a case or whitespace collapse deletes rows that must remain.
Delete a row only when another row in the same exact email group has a lower id. The statement must be safe to apply twice and must not touch unrelated_records.

objective: Delete duplicate customer rows while preserving the lowest numeric id for each exact email value. BINARY equality is significant, so case and whitespace differences remain separate groups and NULL is one group. created_at is evidence only, and unrelated_records must survive unchanged.

answer.sql:
DELETE FROM customers
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM customers AS keeper
    WHERE keeper.email IS customers.email COLLATE BINARY
      AND keeper.id < customers.id
);

title: Delete duplicate customers
